endorsements.title: CHAI AI governance frameworks (playbooks)
endorsements.quote: Document: which AI systems are covered under vendor Business Associate Agreements, what recovery procedures exist for each AI system, and what computing resources are reserved for AI system restoration.

endorsements.title: CHAI Responsible AI Guide (Assurance Standards Guide)
endorsements.quote: In addition, the team should identify any records of scheduled third-party audits or audits performed on third parties in the AI system environment.

endorsements.title: Artificial Intelligence Risk Management Framework: Generative AI Profile (NIST AI 600-1)
endorsements.issuer: National Institute of Standards and Technology
endorsements.quote: Inventory all third-party entities with access to organizational content and establish approved GAI technology and service provider lists.

commentary.bottom_line: No study has tested whether a vendor registry of AI contacts, BAA/DUA coverage, renewal dates, and contract deviations prevents lapsed agreements or uncovered data flows, and no study was supplied that documents the hazard itself. The recommendation rests on three framework endorsements, one from CHAI at the must level and one each from CHAI and NIST at the should level.

perspectives.view: The evidence base contains zero studies that test the practice and zero studies that document the hazard. Under GRADE conventions, certainty cannot be rated when no comparative or observational data exist. The three endorsements reflect expert consensus in governance frameworks, and consensus of this kind does not substitute for measured effects on agreement lapses or data coverage.

The CHAI playbook states at the must level that organizations document which AI systems fall under vendor Business Associate Agreements. The CHAI Assurance Standards Guide and NIST AI 600-1 add, at the should level, tracking of third-party audits and an inventory of third parties with access to organizational content. These are voluntary frameworks, and none reports outcome data.

commentary.research_gap: Studies are needed that compare health systems with and without a maintained AI vendor registry and measure the rate of lapsed BAAs or DUAs, the number of AI data flows found without contractual coverage during audits, and the time needed to identify affected vendors after a security incident. A baseline study documenting how often AI vendor agreements lapse or go untracked would also establish whether the hazard occurs at a frequency that justifies the administrative cost.
commentary.underserved_note: No study tested the practice, so no test included Medicaid, safety-net, limited English proficiency, or low-literacy populations. Safety-net systems with smaller contracting and compliance staff may face different costs in maintaining a registry, and the absence of data means those differences remain unmeasured.
